## LmdbEnv.transactionFast() method

Run a callback inside an off-thread LMDB write transaction.

**Signature:**

```typescript
transactionFast<T>(fn: (tx: LmdbTransaction) => T | Promise<T>): Promise<T>;
```

## Exceptions

[LmdbError](./lmdb.lmdberror.md) if the env is read-only, if the callback calls `tx.abort()`<!-- -->, or if the callback throws — the last case wraps the original error as `cause` and states that the writes were committed.

## Remarks

\*\*SQL equivalent\*\*:

```sql
BEGIN;
-- <writes performed via putSync/removeSync inside fn>
COMMIT;
```
Gives the same atomicity as [LmdbEnv.transaction()](./lmdb.lmdbenv.transaction.md) — one native LMDB write transaction, invisible to other processes until it commits — but the commit is handed to lmdb-js's writer thread instead of blocking the main thread, and it batches with other writes queued in the same event turn.

\*\*The trade-off is rollback, and it is not available here.\*\* lmdb-js's `db.transaction()` records a callback error and rethrows it, but never calls `mdb_txn_abort` — the native transaction commits regardless. So:

- [LmdbTransaction.abort()](./lmdb.lmdbtransaction.abort.md) throws `LmdbError` rather than silently doing nothing. - A callback that throws still propagates the error, but every write it already performed is \*\*committed\*\*, not discarded.

Use [LmdbEnv.transaction()](./lmdb.lmdbenv.transaction.md) whenever the outcome depends on the callback failing partway. Reach for this one when the callback cannot fail partway, or when partial application of a bulk write is harmless (the package uses it for `putMany`<!-- -->, `purgeExpired`<!-- -->, `increment` and CDC pruning).

## Example


```typescript
await env.transactionFast(() => {
  users.putSync("u1", user);
  sessions.putSync("s1", session);
});
```
